language.script_notes: Letters ã, õ, ç, BR-XXX shields, black-backed signs. Higher BR route numbers (200s–400s) run through the region.

road_furniture.bollard_color: No standard bollard, as elsewhere in Brazil.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam where present; many interior roads have none.
road_furniture.line_paint: Interior roads are frequently unmarked or unpaved.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in coastal cities; little kerbing inland.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: The national ladder-and-holes concrete pole. Infrastructure is visibly poorer than the Southeast — more dirt roads, more motorcycles, simpler buildings.

architecture.roof_style: Low-pitched gables; many flat-roofed rendered houses.
architecture.roof_material: Terracotta tile and fibre-cement sheeting; a lot of unfinished builds.
architecture.wall_construction: Rendered or bare masonry; simple single-storey houses inland.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Whitewash and bright colours on the coast; bare brick and sun-bleached render inland.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Colourful Portuguese colonial centres with azulejo tiles on the coast (Salvador's Pelourinho, Olinda, São Luís); plain rendered or brick houses across the sertão.

nature.vegetation: Semi-arid Caatinga in the interior — thorny scrub, columnar cacti, low bushes that drop their leaves in the dry season. A green coastal belt (Zona da Mata) with sugarcane and coconut palms; carnaúba wax palms in Ceará and Piauí, babassu palms toward Maranhão.
nature.terrain: Low uplands 200–500 m (the Borborema, Ibiapaba and Araripe plateaus) inland; a coastal plain with extensive white sand dunes near Natal, Fortaleza and in the Lençóis Maranhenses.
nature.climate_signature: Hot year-round. The interior is markedly dry with low, seasonal rainfall — sparse brown vegetation and often pale, whitish soil rather than the red soil of central Brazil. Intense sun and hard shadows.

vehicles.plate_color: Mercosur white plate with a blue 'BRASIL' strip; many older grey plates; red commercial plates.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Motorcycles are extremely common and often the main vehicle; older, more worn cars than in the south.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mix of Gen 2, Gen 3 and Gen 4.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Reasonable along the coast and main highways, thinner across the sertão. Mostly white car; a lot of unpaved-road coverage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same language, plates, concrete poles and coastal Atlantic Forest
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Northeast interior is dry Caatinga — cacti, leafless scrub, pale soil, poorer unpaved roads; the Southeast is green, hilly, red-soiled and developed.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Both are hotter, poorer and less-covered than the south; motorcycles everywhere
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The North is dense Amazon rainforest and big rivers; the Northeast interior is open dry scrub. Tocantins (dry cerrado) is the fuzzy middle case.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Hot, arid scrub with cacti can resemble northern Mexico
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Language — Portuguese vs Spanish. Mexican plates, road signs, topes and OXXO stores have no Brazilian equivalent; Brazil keeps its ladder-and-holes poles.
